about_page.subtitle: Independent continental indexing and bibliometrics for African scientific research.
about_page.mission_text1: Scholarly journals published in Africa frequently face structural barriers to discovery in global commercial indexing databases. AfriJournal Index was founded to bridge this gap, providing an independent, high-standard indexing platform specifically designed for peer-reviewed journals across all 54 African countries.
about_page.mission_text2: Our platform evaluates quality guidelines fairly, using high-speed automated crawler screening to verify active ISSN registration, double-blind peer-review policies, editorial governance, publication continuity, and continental research contributions without paywalls.
about_page.partner_text: AfriJournal Index operates with complete editorial independence under the guidance of a continental academic advisory board. We adhere strictly to the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) Core Practices, the DOAJ Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing, and open-access mandates to eliminate predatory practices and protect African research integrity.
about_page.pillar_open_text: Zero submission fees, zero subscription paywalls, and zero barriers for African journals and researchers.
about_page.pillar_metrics_text: Objective impact calculation models (AJIF) and citation tracking designed to reflect African scientific advancement.
about_page.pillar_capacity_text: Instant crawler compliance diagnostics helping editorial teams identify and fix metadata deficiencies.

items.q: What is AfriJournal Index?
items.a: AfriJournal Index (AJIF) is an open-access academic indexing and bibliometric platform built specifically for African research journals. We catalog peer-reviewed journals, compute calculated impact factor scores, track citations, and provide researcher profile dashboards — all without paywalls.

items.q: Is AfriJournal Index free to use?
items.a: Yes. Browsing the catalog, searching journals, viewing rankings, submitting a journal for indexing, and registering a researcher profile are 100% free. AfriJournal Index operates as open public infrastructure for African academic scholarship.

items.q: Who governs AfriJournal Index?
items.a: AfriJournal Index is governed by an independent continental academic advisory committee consisting of university scholars, research librarians, and open science advocates across East, West, North, Southern, and Central Africa. The platform maintains strict editorial neutrality and independence.

items.q: Which countries are covered?
items.a: The Platform indexes journals from all 54 African countries. Our regional AJIF score gives proportional weight to publication volume and open access availability within the continent, ensuring journals from all regional research ecosystems are fairly represented.

items.q: How do I submit a journal for indexing?
items.a: Navigate to the Submit page, complete the form with your journal details (name, ISSN, publisher, country, website URL), and submit. You can also use our 1-Click OJS / OAI-PMH Auto-Import to automatically harvest repository metadata.

items.q: How fast is the evaluation process?
items.a: Evaluation is automated via real-time web crawlers and registry verifiers. Technical audits and metadata screening begin immediately upon submission, with crawler audit logs generated in minutes rather than months.

items.q: What does the automated compliance check evaluate?
items.a: Our automated crawlers inspect: domain security and active HTTPS encryption, homepage availability, official ISSN/eISSN registry validity, peer-review policy statements, verifiable editorial board affiliations, and publication frequency continuity.

items.q: Can I track my submission status in real time?
items.a: Yes. After submitting, you receive a unique submission reference ID. You can enter this ID or your journal's registered ISSN on the Status page to view live crawler logs, compliance scores, and indexing decisions.

items.q: What are the minimum criteria to qualify for indexing?
items.a: A journal must have: (1) An active, registered Print ISSN or Online eISSN; (2) A functioning, secure website (HTTPS); (3) A publicly declared double-blind or peer-review policy; (4) An identifiable editorial board with verifiable institutional affiliations; and (5) A minimum publishing history of at least two consecutive issues without multi-year gaps.

items.q: What is the difference between a technical error and an editorial rejection?
items.a: Technical errors (such as temporary server downtime, DNS misconfiguration, or typographical errors in your ISSN) can be corrected and re-tested immediately with zero penalty. In contrast, rejections caused by serious editorial deficiencies (such as unverified editorial boards, missing peer review policies, or suspected predatory practices) require substantive reform.

items.q: What is the 6-month cooling-off period and why does it exist?
items.a: When a submission fails evaluation due to serious editorial or ethical non-compliance, a mandatory 6-month cooling-off period is activated for that ISSN. This standard academic policy ensures that editorial boards have adequate time to publish new regular issues, update policies, and enact genuine governance improvements before re-submitting.

items.q: Can an indexed journal be de-indexed?
items.a: Yes. AfriJournal Index conducts automated continuous monitoring. If an indexed journal becomes defunct, engages in citation manipulation, removes peer-review transparency, or violates academic integrity standards, it will be flagged for editorial review and subject to de-indexing.

items.q: How is the AfriJournal Citation Index (AJCI) calculated?
items.a: The AJCI score is calculated annually using the international standard 2-year citation window (citations in year T to articles published in T-1 and T-2, divided by citable items in T-1 and T-2). The Regional Representation Quotient (RRQ) is reported separately as an uncorrupted percentage of citations from African institutions.

items.q: How do Crossref DOIs and citation tracking work?
items.a: Our indexing system integrates with Crossref metadata APIs. When indexed articles are cited across participating African and international publications, the citation graph is automatically updated.

items.q: How often are rankings and quartiles updated?
items.a: The rankings leaderboard dynamically calculates positions from the database in real time. Official journal citation index reports and subject quartile classifications (Q1–Q4) are updated annually.

items.q: Can I embed a live verification badge on my journal's website?
items.a: Yes. Every verified journal page features an embeddable SVG verification badge that editors can place in their website footer or sidebar, linking directly to their official certificate of indexing.

items.q: How do I create a researcher profile?
items.a: Register for a free account. Once logged in, your profile dashboard displays your verified publication list, citation analytics, and calculated h-index. You can also search the database to claim authored articles.

items.q: How is my h-index calculated?
items.a: Your h-index is computed dynamically based on claimed and verified publications: a researcher has an index h if h of their publications have each received at least h citations.

items.q: What is ORCID and why should I connect it?
items.a: ORCID provides a persistent, globally unique digital identifier that distinguishes you from every other author. Connecting your ORCID enables automated verification of article claims and prevents author disambiguation errors.

items.q: How are university rankings generated?
items.a: The Institutional Leaderboard aggregates total verified publications, total citations, average citations per paper, and the institutional h-index across all affiliated researchers and university press journals.

privacy_page.title: Privacy Policy
privacy_page.subtitle: Your privacy and academic data rights are paramount. This policy outlines how AfriJournal Index handles personal information in compliance with continental and international data standards.
privacy_page.sec1_p1: AfriJournal Index operates as an independent, non-commercial continental academic indexing infrastructure governed by a pan-African scholarly advisory body. We are committed to transparency, open science, and robust data protection.
privacy_page.sec2_p1: We collect information necessary to provide academic indexing and researcher analytics services:
privacy_page.sec2_li1_1: Full name, academic email address, and securely hashed passwords (bcrypt)
privacy_page.sec2_li1_2: Institutional affiliation and primary academic discipline
privacy_page.sec2_li1_5: Contact details provided during editorial inquiries
privacy_page.sec2_li2_1: Journal metadata (title, ISSN/eISSN, publisher, website URL, frequency)
privacy_page.sec2_li2_2: Published article titles, DOIs, abstracts, and author bylines harvested via public OAI-PMH or Crossref feeds
privacy_page.sec2_li2_3: Authorship claims submitted by registered researchers
privacy_page.sec2_li3_1: Server logs (IP address, browser user-agent, request timestamps) for security monitoring
privacy_page.sec2_li3_2: Automated crawler audit logs verifying journal website responsiveness and SSL encryption
privacy_page.sec2_li3_3: Session cookies required strictly for platform authentication
privacy_page.sec3_p1: All collected data is processed strictly for academic and operational purposes:
privacy_page.sec3_li1: Verifying journal eligibility and calculating AJIF citation impact indicators
privacy_page.sec3_li2: Generating researcher profile pages, verified authorship records, and h-index metrics
privacy_page.sec3_li3: Aggregating university-level research outputs for the Institutional Leaderboard
privacy_page.sec3_li4: Communicating evaluation results, crawler audit logs, and account notices
privacy_page.sec3_li5: Detecting and preventing abusive automated traffic or fraudulent claims
privacy_page.sec3_li6: Generating anonymized continental research output analytics
privacy_page.sec3_li7: Maintaining platform security, SSL verification, and system reliability
privacy_page.sec4_p1: We process personal data in adherence with the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention) and internationally recognized data protection principles (including the GDPR where applicable):
privacy_page.sec4_li1: Contractual necessity for providing requested indexing and user account services
privacy_page.sec4_li2: Legitimate academic interest in maintaining transparent, publicly verifiable scientific bibliometrics
privacy_page.sec4_li3: Explicit user consent provided upon registration or editorial inquiry
privacy_page.sec5_p1: In accordance with scholarly communication standards, academic metadata—including journal titles, published article metadata, author names, institutional affiliations, and linked public ORCID IDs—are part of the permanent public scholarly record.
privacy_page.sec5_li1: Public scholarly metadata is discoverable via the open catalog and researcher consoles.
privacy_page.sec5_li2: Personal account credentials and private contact emails are never displayed publicly.
privacy_page.sec5_li3: Researchers may claim or unclaim publications from their profile at any time.
privacy_page.sec5_p2: We do not sell, rent, or lease academic or personal data to third parties under any circumstances.
privacy_page.sec6_p1: AfriJournal Index does not host commercial third-party advertisements, behavioral tracking pixels, or data broker integrations. Your browsing activity on this platform is never monetized or shared with marketing networks.
privacy_page.sec7_p1: We implement robust security safeguards including end-to-end HTTPS encryption, salted bcrypt password hashing, and role-based database access controls. Under applicable data protection regulations, you hold the right to:
privacy_page.sec7_li1: Access: Request a copy of the personal data held about your account.
privacy_page.sec7_li2: Rectification: Correct any inaccurate personal or affiliation details in your profile.
privacy_page.sec7_li3: Erasure: Request the deletion of your user account and personal credentials.
privacy_page.sec7_li4: Restriction: Object to or restrict specific processing of your personal information.
privacy_page.sec7_li5: Data Portability: Request an export of your claimed publication data in standard formats.
privacy_page.sec7_p2: To exercise any of these rights, contact our data protection team via our Contact page or at privacy@afrijournal.org.
